key_insight: Two current-generation large language models, Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6, performed at about 95% accuracy on an anesthesiology in-training examination question bank, including strong results on figure-based items when images were provided.
clinical_relevance: These results suggest LLMs may be useful as high-performing study aids in anesthesiology education, but their value still depends on access to complete question context, especially figures.
method: 1,001 single-best-answer anesthesiology ITE review questions were tested
Each question was given once in a fresh, stateless prompt with no tools, retrieval, or answer key
All 27 figure-dependent items were included; published figures were supplied for image-based testing
evidence_signal: Claude Opus 5 scored 947/1,001 (94.6%) and GPT-5.6 scored 946/1,001 (94.5%); performance was similar overall, but withholding figures from figure-based questions cut pooled accuracy from 88.9% to 52.8%.
watch_item: This was a controlled review-bank evaluation, so real-world educational use may be less reliable if prompts are incomplete, figures are missing, or answer formats differ from the test setting.
paper_title: Assessing the Performance of Artificial Intelligence on Anesthesiology In-Training Examinations and Applicability in Medical Education
